verdict.rationale: Statsig's docs say server SDKs evaluate gates without a network request after initialization, typically in under 1ms, and that the SDKs handle caching. That covers the core of local, no-network-per-check evaluation. However, the docs never describe the server SDKs holding a downloaded ruleset in memory (only the client On-Device Eval SDKs are described that way), and they claim sub-millisecond rather than microsecond latency. missing for 10: explicit documentation that server SDKs download and cache the full ruleset locally, a documented microsecond-level latency figure, independent or hands-on corroboration of evaluation performance

support.subject: As a platform engineer, my server SDKs evaluate flags locally from a cached ruleset — microsecond decisions with no network call per flag check

citations.quote: After initialization, both Client and Server SDKs evaluate experiments/gates _without a network request_, and typically in less than 1ms.
Statsig handles caching, retry mechanisms, and networking.
